sources.entry: LibreChat ⚠ - Enhanced ChatGPT-compatible AI chat interface supporting multiple AI providers, with multi-user auth, message search, and plugin support. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker
LibreChat | ChatGPT-style interface for many AI providers with agents, MCP and multi-user support

summary.one_liner: LibreChat is a self-hosted, ChatGPT-style AI chat platform that connects to many AI providers and adds agents, MCP tool support, multi-user authentication, and message search.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a chat interface supporting Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, Vertex AI, the OpenAI Responses API, and any OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint, plus local and remote providers such as Ollama, Mistral AI, and OpenRouter. It includes LibreChat Agents with Skills, Subagents, MCP server support, file search, and code execution. Other listed features are a sandboxed Code Interpreter API, web search, image generation, Artifacts for React/HTML/Mermaid previews, and conversation branching with presets. Multi-user access uses OAuth2, LDAP, or email login, with an admin panel for users, groups, and roles. It also lists speech-to-text and text-to-speech, resumable streams with Redis, OpenTelemetry and Langfuse observability, and conversation import/export. The README's section on "What's New in v0.8.8" describes release features but does not include install instructions.
use_cases: chat with multiple AI providers in one interface
run AI agents with MCP tools
multi-user AI chat for a team or organization
chat with files and upload images to models
notable: Connects to many AI providers, including OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints without a proxy
Agents with Skills, Subagents, and an Agent Management API
Code Interpreter sandbox supporting many languages, self-hostable via ClickHouse/code-interpreter
Resumable streams and multi-tab sync, scalable with Redis
Admin panel for live configuration and per-role permissions
caveats: Attached code workspaces are described as highly experimental, and the Agent Management API is beta
Breaking changes are noted in the changelog, so the README asks users to check it before updating
The README does not give setup steps; installation details are in the external docs
